prompt: Explain the federal budget using only football metaphors. Do not stop when they stop working.
response:
*cracks knuckles*

Alright, listen up. The federal budget is your team's salary cap, except the cap is made of elastic, dreams, and the ghost of every negotiation since 1789.

**The Budget Process: Preseason**

Every year, the President—your head coach—walks into the owner's box and says "This is our game plan." That's the **budget proposal**. It's like drawing up a playbook where you sign twelve Pro Bowl receivers and also somehow afford a stadium made of gold. The coach knows it won't happen. The owner (Congress) knows it won't happen. But you gotta submit the paperwork or you forfeit the draft.

Then Congress—your **offensive line, except there's 535 of them and none of them agree on the snap count**—takes over. The House and Senate each write their own budget resolutions. It's like having two offensive coordinators who hate each other calling plays simultaneously. The ball is snapped. Chaos reigns. Someone is blocking air. Someone else is tackling their own quarterback.

**Appropriations: The Regular Season**

Twelve appropriations subcommittees divide up the money like position groups fighting for salary cap space. Defense is your quarterback room—gets paid, gets attention, gets the Gatorade commercials. Nobody questions the quarterback money. You suggest cutting quarterback money, you get run out of town on a rail.

Meanwhile, discretionary spending—your special teams and depth pieces—gets shoved in a locker and told "make it work." They're running on veteran minimum contracts and praying nobody gets hurt.

**Mandatory Spending: Guaranteed Contracts**

Here's where it gets sticky. Social Security? Medicare? Those are your **guaranteed contracts, dead cap hits, the money that's already on the books**. You can't cut them. You can restructure, push money around, convert salary to signing bonus and pray the cap goes up later. But the money? It hits. Every year. Like clockwork. Like a punter you overpaid in 2008 who you're still paying through 2035 because of void years and prorated bonuses.

The **debt ceiling**? That's your credit card limit, except you've already bought the stadium, the team plane, and seventeen years of ice baths. Now you're arguing about whether to pay for the things you already bought. You're at the register. The groceries are bagged. You're fighting about whether groceries are good actually. The line behind you stretches to infinity.

**Continuing Resolutions: Running the Same Play**

When Congress can't pass a budget by October 1? **Continuing resolution**. You run the same play as last year. No new schemes. No adjusting to the defense. Just "we'll figure it out later" while the clock runs and the fans boo and the punter is still getting that dead money because of course he is.

Shutdown? That's a **forfeit**. Everyone goes home except the kicker for some reason. The kicker has to show up. Don't ask why. The kicker is essential personnel now. The kicker represents air traffic controllers and nuclear facility inspectors, apparently.

**Reconciliation: The Trick Play**

Sometimes they use **budget reconciliation**—the single-wing, the fumblerooski, the thing you're only allowed to do once a year with simple majority rules. It's messy. It's arcane. It somehow involves the Parliamentarian, who is the referee who only comes out for this one specific play and has a rulebook written in 1974 cursive.

**Deficits and Debt: Cap Hell**

Running a deficit? You're **over the cap**. Pushing money into future years. Converting base salary to signing bonus. Kicking the can until your can-kicker retires and you still owe him money. The national debt is your **accumulated dead cap**—every dollar you pushed, every guarantee you guaranteed, stretching back to when leather helmets were standard issue.

Some years you think "the cap will go up." And it does! GDP growth! Inflation! New TV deals! Except now your star linebacker (healthcare costs) wants a restructure, your left tackle (interest on the debt) is eating more of your cap than planned, and you still haven't fixed the special teams unit (infrastructure) that keeps allowing blocked punts.

**Taxes: Revenue Sharing**

Revenue comes from **taxes**, which fans hate paying even though they want the team to win. "Cut my ticket prices!" they scream. "Also sign better players!" The math doesn't work but try telling them that. Try explaining that the salary floor exists for reasons. They'll throw batteries at you. This is Philadelphia. This is always Philadelphia.

**The CBO: Analytics Department**

The Congressional Budget Office is your **analytics department**. They run the numbers. They say "that trade will cost us $2 billion and three wins." Everyone ignores them. The coach goes with his gut. The gut has been wrong since 1986. The gut doesn't care.

**Lobbyists: Free Agents with Agents**

Lobbyists are **player agents** hanging around the facility. They represent the defense contractors, the pharmaceutical companies, the agricultural subsidies that keep a certain corn-heavy state happy. "My client deserves $50 million guaranteed," they say, about a punter. About a punter who is also a battleship. About a battleship that is somehow a tax break for racehorse depreciation. Don't think about it. The agent gets his 3%.

**The Fed: The League Office**

The Federal Reserve isn't Congress—they're the **league office**. They don't set your roster, but they set the rules everyone plays under. Interest rates are the **competitive balance tax threshold**. Too hot? The rich teams (the economy) spend wild, inflation runs, your dollar (your salary cap space) buys less. Too cold? Nobody signs anyone, the fans get nervous, the stadium goes quiet.

**Entitlement Reform: Trading Your Aging Stars**

Want to reform Social Security? You're **trading the beloved veteran** who led you to the promised land. The fans will riot. They will burn jerseys. They will remember this in 2047 when you're running for the Ring of Honor. Every proposal is "we love him, but..." followed by a restructuring that somehow pays him more later for less now and everyone pretends this solves something.

**The Filibuster: The Two-Minute Warning That Never Ends**

The Senate filibuster is a **two-minute warning where the clock never moves**. You need sixty votes to call a timeout that actually stops the clock. Otherwise? The other team holds the ball. Forever. They huddle. They look at the sideline. They huddle again. The announcers run out of things to say. Your grandchildren are born and die and still third down.

**Emergency Spending: The Hail Mary**

War. Pandemic. Financial crisis. These are your **Hail Marys**, your fourth-and-forever plays where you throw the rulebook out, convert every possible base salary, guarantee everything to everyone, and pray. It works or it doesn't, but the cap consequences come in three years when you're wondering why you can't afford a backup tight end.

**Off-Budget: The Practice Squad That Costs $80 Billion**

Some spending lives **off-budget**—Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, the things that are "technically not on the salary cap" except they totally are when they implode and you have to sign them to the active roster mid-season and pretend you planned for this.

**Baselines: The Moving Goalposts**

Current-law baselines vs. current-policy baselines? Those are your **field goal posts on wheels**. Is the kick good? Depends which baseline you measure from. From here? Wide left. From three yards to the left and adjusted for
